title: Sliding window: S = 256 instead of 1024
description: One character in _compute_window_sizes: short_window = long_window // 2 -> // 8, so the 7 'S' layers attend 256 tokens instead of 1024; layers 3, 7, 9 keep the full 2048. Nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.984406 vs the 0.987227 baseline: -0.00282, ~3.5 sigma on the round-3 arm-to-arm sd of 8e-4, and -0.0041 against the round-3 pool mean (0.9885) which is the fairer bar since the baseline is an order statistic. 1174 steps, 307.8M tokens (+4.7% over baseline's 293.9M), MFU 39.79% (down from 42.03% purely because the FLOP counter drops the attention term - the actual tok/s rose from 973K to 1.02M), peak VRAM 34.6GB, 85.9M params, mean-of-last-60 train loss agrees with val. The window axis now has four points at matched settings: 2048 (all-L, my r3 arm) 0.989734 / 1024 (baseline) 0.987227 / 256 (this) 0.984406, monotone downward - less local attention context is better in this regime and the axis has NOT turned over yet. Two mechanisms are mixed in roughly 2:1 - representational (the 2048-vs-1024 pair was pure representational at near-matched tokens, +0.0025) and throughput (-9.5% FLOPs/token bought +4.7% tokens here, worth maybe -0.001). Next probe is S=128 (long_window // 16), and if that also wins the interesting question is whether the three full-context layers are carrying the whole long-range job, i.e. whether a pattern with even fewer L layers helps.
